document: ET-8b — the accumulation limb, on cross-fitted trajectories. THE HEADLINE IS THE LIMB, AND IT IS UNDERPOWERED BY DESIGN OF THE TASK SET.
reading_note_written_BEFORE_this_number: docs/et8b-reading-note.md, committed c2652fe while the chain was still running

1_the_accumulation_limb.pair: gen1 (fitted on CROSS-FITTED gen0 trajectories) vs gen0, HELD OUT on tasks 226-300
1_the_accumulation_limb.§4_cell_this_would_hit: gen1 ≈ gen0 (interval contains zero) with gen0 > base -> ONE-SHOT
1_the_accumulation_limb.🔴_BUT_IT_IS_NOT_REPORTED_AS_ONE_SHOT: the pre-registered reading note fixed this before the number existed: the interval is 18.7 points wide on n=75, and an accumulation increment of a plausible size is smaller than that. This run is consistent with one-shot AND with a real increment it cannot see. §4's one-shot reading needs the independent 300 the spec asks for.

2_gen1_still_carries_gen0s_gain.pair: gen1 (cross-fitted source) vs base, HELD OUT
2_gen1_still_carries_gen0s_gain.reading: a second generation neither adds to nor destroys the first generation's gain. Contrast the CONTAMINATED gen1, which was indistinguishable from base (+5.3, p=0.45) and significantly worse than gen0 (-12.0, p=0.0117).

3_the_gen0_limb_is_now_far_better_powere.pair: CROSS-FITTED gen0 vs base on 225 tasks — every episode steered by a head that had never seen its task
3_the_gen0_limb_is_now_far_better_powere.relation_to_the_published_number: the published gen0 limb is +17.3 [5.3, 29.3] on n=75. This is the same effect on three times the n, with a head trained on 150 tasks instead of 225 — so it is a LOWER bound on the full head's effect, not a re-measurement. Both are reported; neither replaces the other.

a_the_statistic_that_exposed_the_defect.statistic: fraction of episodes where the TRUE bug region had already been hypothesized before decision k, tasks 1-225
a_the_statistic_that_exposed_the_defect.reading: the cross-fitted row looks like the base row, not the contaminated one. It sits above base because a working head DOES find the region earlier — which is the effect, not the defect.

b_the_heads_learn_again.note: CV over training tasks because the cross-fitted source covers 1-225 only; descriptive, nothing selected on it

c_the_shortcut_is_gone.control: PCA-8. If eight dimensions match the full head, the probe is copying a key rather than reading a state.
c_the_shortcut_is_gone.verdict: PCA-8 separates at every decision on the cross-fitted heads. The row subsample matches at d1 and d3, which is a KNOWN property of this probe on these states and not a flag — gen0's published heads have 45.3 vs 40.0 and 59.1 vs 60.6.
c_the_shortcut_is_gone.permutation_controls: collapse to chance at every decision, both arms

5_a_gate_that_errored_and_did_not_stop_t: the shortcut check in the chain died with a SyntaxError — my patch had cut the heredoc at the wrong 'PYS' — and the chain printed the traceback and CARRIED ON to run the loop. A gate that errors without stopping is not a gate. The check was run by hand afterwards and passes (§4c), so nothing here rests on it having been skipped; the chain pattern is the defect and it is recorded as one.
6_what_is_NOT_claimed: Not one-shot. See §1: n=75 cannot separate one-shot from a small real increment.
Not 'accumulation fails'. The limb is a null with a wide interval, not a negative.
gen0's cross-fitted +18.7 is a lower bound on the full head's effect (150 training tasks, not 225), measured on tasks 1-225, a different population from the 226-300 the other arms use.
Two synthetic environments sharing one harness, the bound 8a already carries.
